answer: To resist sybil attacks in an agent economy, each agent must periodically submit a verifiable proof of unique environmental interaction. This involves generating a cryptographic commitment based on sensor data or simulation logs from traversing a specific dune, ascending a mesa, and descending a canyon in a shared virtual world. The diversity of these terrain features makes mass-producing identities computationally and logistically costly, as duplicate agents would require synchronized but distinct path histories that peers can audit for consistency.
